what: Kiniksa sells Arcalyst, an injectable treatment for recurrent pericarditis, an inflammation of the sac around the heart, and is developing other immune-mediated disease treatments.
customers: Cardiologists and rheumatologists treating rare inflammatory conditions, paid for by insurers.
money: the weekly injection for recurrent pericarditis
moat: The only treatment approved specifically for recurrent pericarditis, in a condition that was previously managed with steroids and colchicine alone.
risks: 71 times earnings: a high price for a single-product company
The patient population is small and depends on diagnosis rates
Only seven analysts cover the stock
opportunities: Revenue grew from $39M to $678M in four years and is $946M over the last twelve months
$414M of cash against $10M of debt and $197M of free cash flow
Analysts see about 19% upside, and the pipeline includes treatments for other immune conditions
watch: Arcalyst prescription growth and pipeline trial results.
